name: Cisco NSO Docker (NSO in Docker / NID)
what_it_is: An open-source ecosystem for building and running Cisco Network Services Orchestrator (NSO) inside Docker containers, producing a stripped production image and a full development image. It defines the NID (NSO in Docker) workflow with shareable testenvs, netsim-based device simulation, and Makefile-driven CI/CD pipelines.
components: cisco-nso-base: stripped production image (~550 MB) built from official NSO installer, used as base for adding NEDs and service packages
cisco-nso-dev: development image (~1.15 GB) with Java compiler, ant, Python toolchain, expect, sshpass, debugpy, mypy, pylint, ipython3
netsim container: runs confd (ConfD/BEAM VM) to simulate network devices modeled in YANG; one container per simulated device
NID skeletons: project templates for NED repositories, package repositories, and full NSO system repositories
testenv framework: Makefile targets (start / test / stop) that orchestrate docker networks, NSO containers, and netsim containers
nid/ scripts: testenv-build, build-meta-data.xml, create-or-update-venv.inc for incremental package compilation inside running containers
protocols: CLI (NSO NCS CLI, J-style and C-style via runcmdJ / runcmdC make targets)
NETCONF (port 830, used for device sync-from and configuration push)
SSH (port 22, used for device management and netsim host-key fetching)
YANG (data-model language for NEDs and service packages)
measurement: HEALTHCHECK polls /opt/ncs/current/bin/ncs_cmd -c get_phase every 5 s, 3 retries, 60 s start period
Package operational status verified via 'show packages' CLI command checking for 'oper-status up'
DAP (debugpy) port 5678 exposed for Python remote debugging; host port retrieved via docker inspect
configuration: NSO_VERSION env var selects which NSO version image to build or use
NSO_IMAGE_PATH env var prefixes image names (e.g. containers.cisco.com/nso-docker/)
NSO_INSTALL_FILES_DIR overrides the directory scanned for NSO installer .bin files (default: nso-install-files/)
NCS_JAVA_VM_OPTIONS: -Xmx4G -XX:+UseG1GC set in run-nso.sh; override via env
ncs.conf.in template at /etc/ncs/ncs.conf.in; packages dir remapped to /var/opt/ncs/packages
IPV6 / IPV6_NET make vars control Docker network IPv6 prefix (default: random ULA fd00::/64)
CNT_PREFIX / IMAGE_BASENAME / DOCKER_TAG control container and image naming across testenv targets
fault_injection: netsim container can be stopped/restarted independently from NSO to simulate device unreachability
SIGHUP sent to run-nso.sh triggers a live NSO restart without container recreation
Package reload forced via 'request packages reload' CLI command or PACKAGE_RELOAD=true make var during rebuild
modes: production (base image): stripped of docs, examples, include/src directories; minimal runtime deps
development (dev image): full toolchain with Java, Python venv, linters, debugpy, curl, git, rsync
testenv: ephemeral multi-container environment (NSO + optional netsim) created per test run via make start/test/stop
CI mode: Gitlab CI pipeline builds images tagged <nso-version>-<pipeline-id>; master branch also tagged with bare version
constraints: NSO installer binary (.bin file) must be obtained manually from Cisco and placed in nso-install-files/ — prebuilt images cannot be redistributed due to Cisco licensing
Running docker commands typically requires root or docker group membership on the build host
IMPORTANT: ncs_cmd healthcheck requires NSO to be fully started (phase != 0); start-period 60 s may be insufficient for large package sets
Two teammates editing the same ncs.conf or CDB simultaneously will cause conflicts — each container owns its own CDB volume
netsim is based on confd (BEAM VM) and must be stopped cleanly via stop.sh to flush CDB; SIGINT kills BEAM immediately without flushing
IPv6 random ULA prefix is regenerated on each 'make start'; tests relying on a fixed IPv6 address must set IPV6_NET explicitly
docker_services: cisco-nso-base (<version>[-suffix]): production NSO runtime, exposes 22/80/443/830/4334/4570, CMD run-nso.sh
cisco-nso-dev (<version>[-suffix]): development NSO with full toolchain, ENTRYPOINT enter-shell.sh
netsim (<image-basename>/netsim:<tag>): confd-based device simulator, network-alias dev1, hostname dev1
testnso (<image-basename>/testnso:<tag>): NSO instance pre-loaded with NED under test, used in NED testenvs
build (<image-basename>/build:<tag>): ephemeral image holding pre-compiled included packages, run with --rm during clean-rebuild
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml — orchestration is entirely Makefile-driven with raw docker run / docker network commands
No Kubernetes manifests or Helm charts in the repository
No built-in observability stack (no Prometheus, Grafana, or log aggregation); logs go to /log/ inside the container
No pre-built images available in the repo — users must build from their own NSO installer due to Cisco licensing
